source.title: From Isolation to Entanglement: When Do Interpretability Methods Identify and Disentangle Known Concepts?
source.authors: Aaron Mueller; Andrew Lee; Shruti B. Joshi; E. Lubana; Dhanya Sridhar; P. Reizinger

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether native neuron dimensions and learned features correspond selectively to known concepts, using correlational disentanglement metrics and probes rather than the Qwen3 neuron-pole audit method.
record.gate_note: The study does not audit positive and negative neuron poles, produce human-readable neuron explanations, or estimate the share of poles with one or two jobs. It does measure DCI-ES disentanglement for the original activation representation of Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B. The paper also reports k-sparse probe comparisons, but those assess concept recovery across multiple dimensions rather than whether each neuron has one main job.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. Its 'Neuron' baseline is the raw residual-stream activation vector at a middle layer, not MLP neurons or neuron poles; Fig. 8 calls it 'residual stream (Neuron)'. It is scored with DCI-ES on four synthetic PCFG concepts. That is concept-level disentanglement of a basis with no privileged neuron axes. It is not a share of neurons with one main job, and it is not an explanation-based or simulation-scored audit. The finding is a related construct and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that SAEs and probes look disentangled under correlational metrics (high D, I, E; low C, meaning feature splitting). Steering a top feature still affects many concepts, despite near-zero interaction effects between features (disjointness R² ≈ 1). So correlational metrics and disjointness do not establish selective steerability. The comparison with 'native neuron-based representation space' refers to raw residual-stream activations, not MLP neurons.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses known concept labels, DCI-ES, MCC, and feature steering on generated text; it does not use the Qwen3 pole audit or tested natural-language neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on featurizer architecture and the degree of cross-concept correlation in the training data. The paper also reports different neuron-baseline performance between Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B in k-sparse concept recovery.

fits_no_version.finding: For four synthetic concepts, the raw residual-stream basis of Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B is reported as less disentangled (D, I, E) than SAE feature spaces. k-sparse probes on residual dimensions need more dimensions to converge in Gemma, while the neuron baseline is strong in Pythia (Fig. 8, Fig. 12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Raw residual-stream dimensions of small LMs are less concept-selective, by DCI-ES, than SAE features for known synthetic concepts.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2025)
record.problems: The benchmark uses generated PCFG text and only four categorical concepts; the authors note that the distribution is narrower than typical SAE training or evaluation data. The paper does not estimate neuron-pole job proportions. The prose summary and Figure 3 caption are not fully consistent about whether all methods achieve high disentanglement.
record.rows_left_out: No additional direct neuron-selectivity outcomes were extracted. The paper's k-sparse probe results measure recovery using multiple dimensions, and its steering results concern SAE features rather than native neuron poles.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job-share percentages.
No share of neurons or poles with one main job in any model. The residual-stream DCI-ES baseline is not a neuron audit.
No comparison of architectures or tools for neuron interpretability.
No attribution graphs built from neurons.
No test of explanations from activating examples.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its V2 'challenges' label are not supported. V2 concerns the share of neuron poles with one main job, judged by explanation. This paper scores residual-stream dimensions (a non-privileged basis) on four PCFG concepts with DCI-ES, with no neuron explanations. The Fig. 3 caption and the §4.2 text also conflict about whether the Neuron baseline scores high, so the row values are unreliable.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit, pole-level analysis, one-job/two-job proportions, or estimate of unexplained poles.

The study tests native neuron representations in Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B on four categorical concepts in generated PCFG text. It does not test dense versus mixture-of-experts comparisons, trillion-parameter models, or the claimed percentages.
No InceptionV1 or cat-and-car example, pose analysis, or recursive-generalization test.
No InceptionV1-sized vision models or estimates of interpretable-neuron shares under different architectures, tools, or regularization.
No attribution-graph evaluation or test of whether model neurons suffice as circuit units without a replacement model.
No explanation generated from activating examples and tested against held-out firing examples.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M
rows.operation_detail: Measured DCI-ES disentanglement for the original activation representation (Neuron, identity featurizer).
rows.measure: DCI-ES disentanglement (D) of native neuron dimensions
rows.value: The text says D, I, and E were high for SAE architectures but not for the original representation space; no numeric D value for the native representation is stated.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 3 reports shaded regions representing 1 standard deviation across 3 training seeds; no numeric uncertainty for this result is stated.
rows.note: This is a concept-level disentanglement measure, not a count of neuron poles with one main job. The prose summary and Figure 3 caption describe the results differently about whether all methods have high disentanglement; the row records the section's explicit statement about the original representation.
rows.check: The subject is Pythia-70M residual-stream dimensions at layer 3, not MLP neurons or poles. DCI-ES disentanglement over four PCFG concepts does not measure V2's share of neurons with one main job. No numeric D value is stated. The Fig. 3 caption says 'All methods achieve high disentanglement', while §4.2 says this does not hold for the original space, so the value cannot be read reliably.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Native neuron representations of Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B on the tested PCFG concept task
reader_labels.reason: The paper states that DCI-ES disentanglement was not high for the original activation representation, unlike the SAE architectures (R1, R2); this is evidence against strong neuron-level concept selectivity in these tested settings.
